{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — IBM e-business Hosting Agreement (Base Terms)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Agreement (Customer: Bluefly) 
**Status:** 19 rules assessed — 9 deviations, 2 missing clauses, 7 compliant, 1 rule benefiting us noted as better-than-preferred

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the Base Terms against our playbook. The commercial architecture is workable, but there are two critical failures and several material ones that we should not sign around.

The two critical points are risk allocation. First, § 8.2(a)(3) requires us to indemnify IBM against any Services Recipient claim "related, directly or indirectly, to the Services" — a one-way customer indemnity for the vendor's own services, relieved only where IBM acted in bad faith, wilfully, with gross negligence or in breach, so we remain exposed for IBM's ordinary negligence and service defects. IBM's own IP indemnity in § 8.1 sits at our fallback and we are not reopening it. Second, the liability cap in §§ 9.1–9.2 is mutual and appropriately sized, but the only carve-outs are indemnification payments and bodily injury/tangible property; confidentiality, data protection and security breaches are affirmatively capped (and § 9/§ 10 are stated to prevail over the confidentiality agreement), with no carve-out for gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or IP infringement. We propose a single mutual "Excluded Claims" sentence rather than reopening the cap.

Beyond those, four issues drive the balance of our exposure: uncapped early termination charges gating our convenience exit (§ 3.4(b)), which IBM can also change unilaterally under § 13.1; a multi-year auto-renewal with a 90-day exit window (§ 3.2); vendor-owned deliverables by default with a licence back that does not permit modification or sublicensing (§ 7.0/§ 5.4); and an expressly revocable licence to Base Components that does not reach our Affiliates or contractors (§ 12.1). Two clauses are absent altogether: post-termination transition assistance and Content return/deletion, and any vendor insurance obligation — significant for a provider hosting our environment and holding our Content. The warranty position is also thin: a reasonable-care services warranty with no deliverable conformance warranty, no warranty period and no remedy, undercut by the "AS IS" disclaimer in § 5.4(c).

On the positive side, the Agreement imposes no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-purchase or non-solicitation obligation on us; § 14.16 (Freedom of Action) affirmatively preserves our freedom to buy comparable hosting elsewhere. New York law is our preferred governing law and there is no arbitration or foreign venue. IBM has no audit right against us at all, which is better than our preferred position — we should not insert an audit framework and inadvertently create one.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Issue / position |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 8.1 Indemnification by IBM (and § 8.2) | IBM's IP indemnity sits at our fallback and is not redlined. § 8.2(a)(3) creates a one-way customer indemnity for claims related directly or indirectly to IBM's own Services; § 8.2(c) relieves us only for IBM's bad faith, wilful misconduct, gross negligence or breach. Narrow to Content and our breach of applicable law, excluding claims arising from IBM's performance. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 9.1 IBM's Limitation of Liability | Cap basis, mutuality and the § 10 consequential-damages exclusion meet or exceed fallback. Carve-outs cover only indemnification payments and bodily injury/tangible property; confidentiality and data obligations are expressly capped. Add a mutual uncapped Excluded Claims provision (confidentiality/data protection, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) as new § 9.3. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 14.10 Assignment | Restriction is one-directional: only our assignment is limited, IBM may assign freely including to a competitor. Add an affiliate carve-out for us and mirror the consent requirement on IBM, with a no-competitor limit. |
| High | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 5.4 Other Disclaimers (with § 7.0) | Materials default to Type II (IBM-owned); licence back is use-only within our Enterprise, with no right to modify or sublicense, and our ownership of Content and Customer Components is never confirmed. Default Materials to Type I, broaden the Type II licence, and add a Customer ownership statement. IBM's pre-existing Materials and Base Components left intact. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience | § 3.4(b) early termination charges are open-ended (quantum left to Attachment A, which IBM may change on 90 days' notice under § 13.1) with no sole-remedy language. Cap at three months' charges for the terminated Services as the sole amount payable and IBM's sole remedy. § 3.3 helpfully disapplies the charges where IBM is in breach. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 12.1 License | Grant is expressly "revocable" with no standard, and runs to Customer only (§ 14.17 confirms no implied licences), excluding Affiliates and contractors. Extend to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf; make revocation available only on termination for our uncured material breach. Fallback: Affiliates on written notice. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No exclusivity, sole-source or requirements obligation; § 14.16 confirms each party may contract with others. Preferred position met. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No non-compete, field-of-use or territory restriction on us; § 14.11 (No Resale) and the § 12.1/§ 14.17 licence limits are ordinary scope boundaries. Preferred position met. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § 3.2 Renewal | Auto-renews for a term equal to the previous term (so multi-year renewals) on 90 days' non-renewal notice; no reminder and no uplift cap. Move to 12-month renewals, 30-day exit notice, 60-day reminder and CPI/3% uplift cap; fallback 60 days with a 5% cap. |
| Medium | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience | Our one-month convenience right and the absence of any IBM convenience right both exceed our preferred position. Failure is exit cost: uncapped § 3.4(b) charges and no refund of prepaid Charges in § 3.5. Cap at three months' recurring Charges and add a pro-rata refund; notice period and Attachment A mechanic left intact. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 5.1 IBM Representations and Warranties | Reasonable care and skill plus compliance with laws, but no conformance warranty for Deliverables/Materials, no warranty period and no remedy; § 5.4(c) puts all Materials, including Type I, "AS IS". Add a 90-day conformance warranty with no-malicious-code assurance and re-perform/repair/refund remedy, and carve express warranties out of the AS IS disclaimer. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Exit assistance and data return | Missing | § 3.5 (Effect of Termination) | § 3.5 addresses only our payment obligations; no transition assistance, data return/export or deletion obligation anywhere. Insert the preferred exit clause into § 3.5, which is already carried by the § 14.2 survival list. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 11.3 Suspected Violations | No audit, inspection or verification right against us anywhere; § 11.3 is only an investigation/remedy right with no access to our systems, personnel or records. Better than preferred — do not insert an audit framework. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 14.3 Choice of Law | New York substantive law (preferred); no arbitration and no foreign or vendor-home venue. Absence of an express exclusive-venue designation is noted, not redlined. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | § 4.1 Charges | No pricing-parity, best-price or offer-matching obligation on us; § 14.16 preserves freedom of action. Preferred position met. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume | Compliant | § 4.1 Charges | No minimum, take-or-pay or shortfall charge; § 11.5 leaves capacity changes to our determination and § 3.4 gives an unconditional monthly exit. Diligence note: check Attachment A / Service Option Attachments and Order Forms for committed spend and the termination-charge formula when issued. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 14.8 Personnel | No non-solicit, no-hire or anti-recruitment covenant on us; § 14.8 covers supervision and subcontracting only. Preferred position met. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 14.12 Risk of Loss | No insurance obligation anywhere, for a provider operating our hosting environment and holding Customer Components. Insert a new § 14.12A at the preferred position (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request); fallback E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M. |

## Walk-away items

These sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and should be resolved before signature:

1. **Customer indemnity for IBM's own Services — § 8.2(a)(3).** A one-way indemnity covering Services Recipient claims related directly or indirectly to the Services, with relief only for IBM's bad faith, wilful misconduct, gross negligence or breach, leaves us carrying IBM's ordinary negligence and service defects.
2. **Revocable licence — § 12.1.** The Base Components licence is expressly revocable with no standard for revocation, meaning IBM can withdraw the licence at discretion.
3. **Multi-year auto-renewal — § 3.2.** Renewal for a term equal in duration to the previous term, so a multi-year initial term rolls into a further multi-year commitment.
4. **No vendor insurance — absent (nearest provision § 14.12 Risk of Loss).** No insurance obligation for a vendor that hosts our environment and processes our data.

We also flag that the warranty position (§ 5.1 read with the § 5.4(c) AS IS disclaimer) approaches walk-away territory: no conformance warranty, no period and no remedy of any kind.

## Next steps

1. Issue the redline covering the nine deviations and two missing clauses, leading with § 8.2(a)(3) and the § 9.3 Excluded Claims sentence as our non-negotiables. We are not reopening IBM's § 8.1 IP indemnity or the size of the § 9.1/§ 9.2 cap.
2. Bundle the three termination-economics points (§ 3.2 renewal, § 3.4(b) early termination charges, § 3.5 refund and exit assistance) into a single negotiation, with the three-months cap and sole-remedy language as our position.
3. Obtain Attachment A, the Service Option Attachments and the Order Forms and re-run the minimum-commitment and termination-charge checks; the Base Terms are compliant on commitments, but the quantum of early termination charges and any committed spend live in those schedules, and § 13.1 lets IBM change Attachment A on 90 days' notice.
4. Ask the business to confirm whether Affiliates and contractors will use the Services, so we can size the § 12.1 licence extension and decide between the preferred grant and the notice-based fallback.
5. Request IBM's certificates of insurance alongside the § 14.12A insert.
6. Leave the audit, governing law, exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-commitment and non-solicitation provisions as drafted; raising them would only risk importing obligations we do not currently carry."}
